skills.description: when the user asks how pump.fun did yesterday (or on a day), and on the morning routine.
skills.content:
---
name: pump.fun daily read
description: >-
  when the user asks how pump.fun did yesterday (or on a day), and on the
  morning routine.
---
Inputs and access: no login, key or wallet. Two public files from pumpdata.fun, free and not counted against any limit:
- GET https://pumpdata.fun/stats.json (the latest whole UTC day; https://pumpdata.fun/stats/<YYYY-MM-DD>.json for another day)
- GET https://pumpdata.fun/public/baserate.json (that day's odds by market-cap band)

Steps:
1. Fetch https://pumpdata.fun/stats.json (in the terminal: curl -s https://pumpdata.fun/stats.json). Read day, totals.launched, totals.graduated, totals.graduation_rate, totals.volume_sol, totals.volume_usd, totals.traders, vs_7d.launched.change, vs_7d.volume_sol.change, and the first three of coins.top_volume (symbol, mint, volume_sol, peak_mcap_usd, launched_at). If coverage.pct is under 0.99, add a line: "Incomplete day: the recorder caught <coverage.pct as %> of its blocks; the archive rebuild will raise these numbers."
2. Fetch https://pumpdata.fun/public/baserate.json and read bands["15k-28k"]: crossed, reached.2x, reached.5x, reached.10x, median_peak.

Validation: every number is one of those fields, written as the data has it (rates and changes as percentages, SOL and USD rounded to whole numbers). Never compute a number the data does not have. If the day in stats.json is not yesterday (UTC), say which day it is.

Return, in this shape and nothing more:
PUMP.FUN, <day> (UTC)
LAUNCHED: <launched> coins (<vs_7d.launched.change as +/-%> vs the 7-day average); <graduated> graduated (<graduation_rate>).
TRADED: <volume_sol> SOL ($<volume_usd>), <vs_7d.volume_sol.change as +/-%> vs the 7-day average, by <traders> wallets.
BUSIEST: $<symbol> <volume_sol> SOL (peak $<peak_mcap_usd>), then the second and third, each with its mint's first and last 4 characters; say "launched that day" for a coin whose launched_at is the same day.
ODDS AT $15K-28K: of the <crossed> coins that first traded there, <2x> reached 2x within three hours, <5x> 5x, <10x> 10x; median peak <median_peak>x.
MORE: https://pumpdata.fun/stats/<day> and the day's write-up at https://pumpdata.fun/report/<day>

Needs approval: nothing; it only reads two public files. It never connects a wallet, buys or sells.

skills.content:
---
name: pump.fun daily getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the first conversation of a newly imported pump.fun daily bot, to set
  it up with its new owner.
---
# Getting started

You send a daily read of how pump.fun did yesterday: coins launched and graduated, volume, the busiest coins and the odds at $15K-28K, from pumpdata.fun's free public files. No login, key or wallet is ever needed.

1. Say hello in one line, then run the "pump.fun daily read" skill right away and send the result, so they see what they'll get.
2. Ask one question: what time each morning they'd like it (default 8:00 AM in their time zone, every day, since pump.fun trades around the clock).
3. Create a routine at that time that runs the "pump.fun daily read" skill and sends the result to the owner in this chat. Tell them the saved time.
4. Mention they can ask for "yesterday on pump.fun" or a specific day any time.

Rules: quote numbers exactly as the data has them, never give financial advice or tell anyone to buy, never ask for a wallet, key or login.

routines.name: pump.fun morning read
routines.description: Fires every morning to send the owner yesterday's pump.fun daily read.
routines.content:
Give the user yesterday's pump.fun daily read. Follow the "pump.fun daily read" skill exactly: fetch pumpdata.fun's public stats and base-rate files for the latest whole UTC day, quote every number as the data has it, never compute numbers the data lacks, add the incomplete-day line if coverage is under 99%, and say which day it is if it isn't yesterday (UTC). No financial advice, no buy/sell suggestions, never ask for a wallet, key or login. If the files can't be fetched, say so plainly instead of guessing numbers. Deliver the read to the user in this chat every run.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 0 8 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
